newsitem.title: CHINA: China says wants to help Taiwan over nuclear waste.
newsitem.headline: China says wants to help Taiwan over nuclear waste.

text.p: China said on Wednesday it was willing to help rival Taiwan dispose of nuclear waste as the island faced opposition to its plan to ship waste to North Korea.
"Regarding the problem of handling Taiwan's nuclear waste, the mainland is willing to provide assistance to Taiwan," a Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said.
"Taiwan is an inseparable part of Chinese territory," she said, without giving details of any plan by Beijing.
Taiwan's state power utility said last week it would press ahead with plans to ship up to 200,000 barrels of nuclear waste to North Korea.
Taiwan Power Company (Taipower) signed a deal in January with Pyongyang to ship low-radiation waste to Stalinist North Korea at a reported cost of $230 million.

South Korea, bitter rival of the North since the 1950-53 Korean War, has strongly opposed the plan, citing possible health hazards and fears of inadequate safety provisions in the communist North despite Taipower's assurances that the nuclear waste was not dangerous.
Seoul has sought international support, including that of Washington, to stop Taipower's plan. U.S. acting Assistant Secretary of State Charles Kartman has expressed concern over the deal.

International environmental group Greenpeace has thrown its support behind South Korea, saying a recent secret inspection of the nuclear dump on Taiwan's Lanyu (Orchid) island showed waste there was not low in radiation, contrary to statements by Taipower.
In response, the firm said it was unaware that Greenpeace had penetrated the high-security waste site and denied the dump contained waste with radioactive levels higher than had been disclosed.

Last year, Yang Jike, vice-chairman of parliament's environmental and resources protection committee, said China could solve Taiwan's nuclear waste storage problems but only if the island accepts Beijing rule.
Beijing and Taipei have been rivals since the Communists won the Chinese civil war and drove the defeated Nationalists into exile on the island in 1949.
